title: North Dakota AI Laws

reading.body:
North Dakota's only AI-related law is a political-advertising disclosure rule, not a regulation of AI development, data centers, or power use.

The law, HB1167, passed on 2025-04-11, requires a prominent disclaimer on political communications and advertising that contain digital content created in whole or in part with artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human. It exempts AI used for text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content when no new impersonation is created, and it defines artificial intelligence for that purpose.

The pattern is narrow and familiar. The state regulates a downstream use, synthetic impersonation in campaign material, and leaves the upstream layers untouched. Nothing in the enrolled text addresses compute, facilities, or electricity, so this law does not constrain where AI is built or how much power it draws.

That is also the limit of what this data says. One law is a single data point, and it covers disclosure in political speech only. It does not indicate how North Dakota treats AI in employment, health care, government procurement, or utility planning, and it says nothing about the data centers and grid demand that dominate AI's physical footprint.

North Dakota has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in North Dakota

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB1167: Artificial intelligence disclosure statements. passed 2025-04-11

    This North Dakota law requires a prominent disclaimer on political communications and advertising that contain digital content created in whole or in part with artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human. It exempts certain uses of artificial intelligence for text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation. It defines artificial intelligence for this purpose.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for North Dakota. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
